lines.speaker: e
lines.text: Scientists from Los Alamos and Sandia came to Taos to hunt a sound most people there cannot hear.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: Hearers said it throbbed like an idling diesel engine.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: New Mexico's congressmen had asked for the hunt. An Air Force lab joined in.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: The team set out microphones, seismic sensors, and magnetometers.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: They caught lightning, the power grid, and a tunneling gopher. No hum.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: Hearers matched it to tones from about thirty-three to eighty hertz.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: In nineteen ninety-three, their ear expert ruled out tinnitus. He wondered if their ears were making the sound.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: But in twenty twenty-six, a study of twenty-eight hearers blamed tinnitus, for many, not all.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: It found no sounds coming from their ears, either.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: And it couldn't rule out a real hum out there.
